title: Post a packet fully through a drop box's flap slot, where the hand cannot follow it in
instruction: Post the brown packet into the drop box.
context: Couriers, delivery robots and staff leave packets, returns and keys in locked drop boxes after hours; one left stuck in the slot is easily taken or soaked and holds the flap open. Unlike turning a board end-on through a doorway or inserting a rod deep into an open box, here the box's front stops the hand, so where the packet is held decides whether it drops in or whether it must be pushed again after letting go.
setup: 'In front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Drop box (fixed): its front is a cream painted wooden panel 20 mm thick (36.0 to 38.0 cm in front of the bases), 360 mm wide (6 cm right to 30 cm left of the midline) and 260 mm tall, standing on the table. Slot through it: 200 mm wide (2 to 22 cm left of the midline), floor 140 mm and ceiling 200 mm above the table. Flap (brass-coloured plate, 210 mm wide, 66 mm tall, 3 mm thick, 50 g, built as in fidelity): on the outer face, hinged along a line 204 mm up, hanging over the slot; it swings inward up to 83 degrees and is pulled shut by its weight and a spring of 0.005 N m per rad, with hinge damping 0.005 N m s per rad. Behind the panel the box is closed (grey painted wood): 220 mm deep inside (38 to 60 cm), 340 mm wide inside, 10 mm side walls, back wall and roof (roof 260 to 270 mm up) and a 5 mm smooth floor board; the only way in is the slot. Packet (loose, brown cardboard box): 160 x 60 x 25 mm, 100 g, lying flat on the table, long side front to back, centred 22.0 cm in front of the bases and 12 cm left of the midline (its far end 60 mm short of the panel). Friction, static / sliding: packet 0.4 / 0.3; panel, flap and box 0.3 / 0.25. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Score 1.0: the whole packet is inside the drop box (no part of it in the slot or in front of the panel's inner face), it is at rest, and the flap is shut: its lower edge is no more than 5 mm inside the panel's outer face. Score 0 for everything else: the packet on the table or anywhere outside the box, stuck in the slot (flat or tilted, partly outside), on top of the box, inside the box with the flap more than 5 mm open, or still moving. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the state at the last step.
reset_notes: 1. Lift the drop box's roof and take the packet out. 2. Lay the packet flat on the table, long side front to back, centred 22.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 12 cm left of the midline (its far end 60 mm short of the panel). 3. Put the roof back. 4. Check that the flap hangs shut, its lower edge against the panel's outer face. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Every part is rigid; the packet is a rigid box. The flap is not solid brass (that would weigh about 350 g): it is 3 mm cast acrylic, 210 x 66 mm, with brass-effect film, 50 g within 2 g with anything fixed to it (about 51 g as built; weigh it). It hangs on pins in the box sides with the stated spring and damping. The front is a 20 mm panel, slot 140 mm up. Friction values are typical of cardboard on painted wood, not measured.
